# Game model (SOLVED 8/8)

## Core rule
Each level has geometric SHAPES (made of straight line segments) and colored DOTS.
WIN when every dot lies ON a line/edge of a shape **of the same color**.

## Coordinates
Board = 64x64 cells of 8px (cell c -> pixel 8c+4). Bottom row is a UI bar.
One move = 3 cells = 24px. Shape edges/centers stay on the 3-cell lattice.

## Actions
ACTION1/2/3/4 = up/down/left/right (move the SELECTED shape).
ACTION5 = cycle selection (white pixel marks the selected shape's center).

## Shape types & invariants
- PLUS: a vertical line (fixed length) + a horizontal line (fixed length).
- X: two diagonals; DIAMOND: |dc|+|dr| = const; LINE: single segment.
- RECTANGLE/SQUARE outline: (width + height) in cells is CONSERVED (e.g. 26).
  Squeezing width by 3 grows height by 3 and vice versa. Min width/height = 4.
- Shapes may extend off-board (clipped); board edges never block.

## Palette squares (recolor)
5x5 or 6x6 gray-bordered colored squares. If ANY cell of a shape overlaps one
(border counts), the shape takes that color. Passing over several is ambiguous —
make sure the LAST/only palette touched is the wanted one.
Rows of palettes act as a color barrier: cross them only through gaps between
palettes (shape must be narrow enough to fit the gap).

## Ring / blocker objects
Solid gray blocks (5x5 or 8x8 with a hole). They BLOCK any line segment whose new
cells would overlap them; other segments of the same shape still move => shapes
DEFORM:
- plus: V and H lines get an offset from each other (blocked one stays behind).
- rectangle: blocked edge stays, opposite edge moves => width/height trade (perimeter conserved).
Growth direction (which side expands) alternates/varies — verify after each step.
To GROW a dimension the shape must straddle the ring (blocked edge on far side of motion).

## Solving procedure
1. Read the board with read_pixels (16 views of 128x128 at 8px sampling works well).
2. Locate dots per color; derive the required shape geometry:
   - two dots sharing a column/row => plus center; 4 dots on a rectangle => rect corners/edges.
3. Check each shape's size/type can satisfy its dot set; assign colors accordingly.
4. Plan: recolor trip (avoid stray palettes), deformations at rings, then final placement.
5. Verify each move's blocking/palette contacts BEFORE moving; costs are 1 action per move.

[After action · message]
**Game complete — WIN, 8/8 levels.**

Final summary of the game model I built and used:

- **Goal:** every colored dot must lie on a line/edge of a shape of the *same color*.
- **Controls:** ACTION1–4 move the selected shape by 24px (3 cells); ACTION5 cycles selection.
- **Progressive mechanics discovered:**
  1. **L1–3:** position crosses/X/diamonds/lines so their arms pass through their dots.
  2. **L4–5:** shape color must match dot color; touching a **palette square** recolors a shape (legend pairs opposite palette positions).
  3. **L6–7:** a gray **ring** blocks individual line segments, so shapes *deform* — pluses offset their arms, rectangles trade width for height (perimeter conserved).
  4. **L8:** combined everything — a full row of palettes formed a color barrier that could only be crossed through narrow gaps, requiring the squares to be squeezed to 4-wide, ferried up, reshaped at a second ring, recolored, and reshaped again into the exact 7×19 and 16×10 rectangles whose corners land on the yellow and pink dots.
